segments.text: Let's walk through this proof: All horses are the same color. Base case: A single horse is always the same color as itself.
Assume the property holds for n horses.
In a set of n+1, the last n horses are the same color. Application of inductive hypothesis to a subset of size n.
The first n horses are also the same color. Application of inductive hypothesis to a different subset of size n.

Wait! If n=1, there is no overlap between {h1} and {h2}! The overlap argument fails when n=1 (moving to n+1=2). For n=1, the first group is {h2} and the second is {h1}. There is no common horse to link the colors of h1 and h2.
